subject: Finalizing p50/p95 targets & measurement window for Brightline go-live
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@brightline.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops <ops@brightline.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 14:23:00 -07:00
Subject: SLO alignment request ahead of Jul 30 go-live

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the detailed onboarding workshop this week — the team found the throughput/latency walk-through useful. We need to lock the SLO commitments for our production cutover on July 30. Specifically:

- Agreed p50 and p95 latency targets for the Hosted API (per-request, text generation endpoint).
- How you plan to measure (rolling windows vs. fixed-day windows), sample granularity, and any carveouts for maintenance/burst events.
- The evidence package you can provide during procurement (sampling CSVs, historical percentiles for similar workloads).

Attached is a brief doc from our side outlining the compliance checklist and internal approval deadlines (brightline_slo_draft_20260716.pdf). Can you share a proposed SLO stanza we can include in the contract addendum and a short list of what you need from our side to accept temporary deviations?

Best,
Maria
Maria Gomez
Head of Platform Reliability
Brightline

Attachments: brightline_slo_draft_20260716.pdf
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@brightline.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLO alignment request ahead of Jul 30 go-live

Maria — thanks for the note and the doc. Putting an initial proposal below (we focused the numbers on your workload profile from the PoC traces):

Proposed SLO stanza (hosted API, per-request)
- p50 <= 140 ms
- p95 <= 420 ms
- Measurement: rolling 30-day window for contractual reporting, 24-hour rolling window for operational alarms
- Sampling granularity: 1-minute aggregation buckets, sampled at request level (no probabilistic sampling; all prod requests counted)
- Exclusions: planned maintenance windows (pre-notified >= 72h), region-level cloud provider outage (documented), and an automatic transient-carveout for single-minute spikes when coincident with autoscaling events (internal detection).

Evidence we can provide for procurement:
- Per-minute percentile CSVs for last 90 days from our hosted test fleet (compressed) — sample: latency_evidence_q2.csv
- Runbook excerpt describing the autoscaling/fallback chain and how model-fallbacks affect tail latency
- A brief canary plan for the first 72h post-cutover with rollback criteria

Temporary deviation / exception requests
- We will accept a documented exception flow where Brightline requests a temporary p95 relief window (up to 7 days) with pre-approved mitigation (traffic throttling or switch to lower-cost throughput variant). Exception requests must include: start/end time, reason, and acceptance of a short joint post-mortem.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm whether the p50/p95 values above match your SLA tolerance.
2) We prepare a 1-page addendum for legal with the wording above.
3) You share any procurement timing constraints (DocuSign deadline).

I attached a small sample CSV extract in this thread for context (latency_evidence_q2.csv). Happy to tighten numbers if your QA workload shows a different distribution.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SLO alignment request ahead of Jul 30 go-live

Looping in a couple of quick clarifications from contract and product sides — copying Maria so Brightline sees our intent.

Karthik, two asks before we finalise the addendum wording:
1) Sampling & partial-aggregation: you note \"all prod requests counted\" — can we clarify that per-minute buckets will be used to compute percentiles, and that we will drop minutes with < 10 requests from percentile aggregation (to avoid noisy single-request minutes). If Brightline has low-volume endpoints, they can be excluded or we can define a per-route SLO separate from global API SLO.
2) Transient carveout criteria: the autoscale-detected spikes carveout needs a short deterministic trigger (example: >3 consecutive 1-min buckets where p99 > threshold AND auto-scale event recorded). We should include the trigger in the addendum to avoid post-hoc disputes.

Also — procurement asked whether we can provide the evidence CSVs as a signed snapshot (to be uploaded to their legal portal) and whether DocuSign will be used for the addendum. If Brightline can confirm DocuSign preference and the portal upload email, we'll route accordingly.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Product Strategy, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this looks good and close to what we expected. Quick responses to the clarifications: 

1) Per-minute bucket rule: Brightline accepts the \"drop minutes with < 10 requests\" rule for global SLOs. We will list high-value low-volume routes separately in the appendix and agree per-route SLOs later.
2) Transient carveout trigger: Accept the deterministic trigger you proposed. Please include the exact thresholds in the addendum (we'll review with our SREs).
3) Procurement process: we prefer DocuSign for signing and will expect an evidence snapshot upload to our legal portal (portal-upload@brightline.com).

Please go ahead and draft the 1-page addendum with the exact trigger language and upload the evidence snapshot (latency_evidence_q2.csv) to the portal. Once we have the addendum, we'll route for signature — target signing by Friday, Jul 23.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Maria

Brightline
